applicability.rationale: Ordinary deterministic application evidence for C05; independent classification review remains pending.

expected.given: A filtered session (Contradictions or Unsupported selected) is displayed with the page mounted. The destination session's ledger query data is already cached, with a different ordered fact set that includes at least one fact the previous filter would hide. A commit-level recorder is installed before navigation: the test renders SessionPage inside a React Profiler whose onRender callback runs synchronously in the commit phase, before passive effects flush, and snapshots the DOM at every commit, together with a probe inside the router that records the current route session id. A MutationObserver drained with takeRecords may corroborate it but does not replace it.
expected.when: Navigate to the destination session without remounting the page, let all pending effects flush, then navigate back to the first session. Each recorded commit stores the route session id, every control's aria-pressed value and displayed count, and the ordered card texts.
expected.then: In the first recorded commit whose route session is the destination, All has aria-pressed=true, Contradictions and Unsupported have aria-pressed=false, the control counts equal counts computed independently from the destination facts, and the cards are exactly all destination facts in supplied order. No recorded commit for the destination session shows aria-pressed=true on Contradictions or Unsupported, or filtered cards or counts. Returning to the first session records the same All-first behavior for that session, and every later session change does likewise. An assertion made only after act() has flushed effects does not satisfy this case.
expected.forbidden: A previous session filter leaking into any committed state of another session, including a transient state that a later effect corrects; relying on a post-act assertion that cannot distinguish an effect-based reset from a derived reset.
counterexamples: Rendering a cached destination session as Unsupported fails.
A reset performed in an effect after the first destination commit passes a post-act assertion but fails here, because its first recorded destination commit still applies the previous filter.

expected.given: The ledger and all three controls are rendered in real Chromium through the labelled synthetic demo entry, started by the existing launcher `python3 scripts/demo-local.py --no-open` and driven by the declared dev-only Playwright runner (`@playwright/test`, Chromium) over the unchanged public fixture. A zero-count category is exercised in the same browser by fulfilling only the ledger request with separate synthetic data in which every fact has a citation and none contradicts. Vitest, jsdom and Testing Library assertions cover accessible names, counts and aria-pressed, but jsdom does not satisfy any focus-rendering or contrast obligation. Before implementation, the same runner records a baseline of the unmodified sidebar and fact cards.
expected.when: From the focusable element immediately before the controls, press Tab repeatedly, then press Enter and separately Space on each control. Hover each control. Measure computed styles in the unfocused, hovered, focused, selected and selected-and-focused states, including a zero-count control.
expected.then: (1) Tab order is All, then Contradictions, then Unsupported, by accessible name of the active element at each step. (2) The three controls are native buttons whose accessible names contain the label and count, and exactly one has aria-pressed=true after each activation. (3) Enter and Space each update the cards and selected state, and the activated button remains the focused element and the same DOM node after the view changes. (4) The focused button's computed outline-style is not none and outline-width is at least 2px, or it has a non-none box-shadow ring of at least 2px, and that indicator differs from the same button's unfocused computed values; outline:none with no replacement fails. (5) Using WCAG relative luminance with each background alpha-composited over its effective ancestor backgrounds, label and count text meets at least 4.5:1 in the unfocused, hovered, focused and selected states, and the focus indicator meets at least 3:1 against the adjacent background; the selected state's computed style differs from the unselected state's in addition to aria-pressed. (6) Existing sidebar and card styling is preserved: the aside's computed width, background, border and the resolved root values of --cit-bg-1, --cit-portal, --cit-flare, --cit-alarm, --cit-text, --cit-text-dim and --cit-hairline, and every fixture card's computed background, border, box-shadow and text color, equal the pre-implementation baseline. (7) Retained evidence is the runner's JSON report, a measurements JSON listing each measured value and threshold, and one screenshot per measured state, copied under docs/12/browser-evidence/ with SHA-256 hashes. If Chromium or the runner cannot be installed or launched, the browser portion of this case is blocked with concrete evidence and is never satisfied by jsdom assertions.
expected.forbidden: Pointer-only interaction, ambiguous selected state, lost focus, outline:none without an equivalent indicator, contrast below the stated thresholds, altered existing sidebar or card styling, or treating jsdom assertions or a screenshot alone as evidence of focus rendering or contrast.
counterexamples: A color-only selected style without aria-pressed fails.
A button with outline:none and no replacement indicator fails the focus-indicator measurement even though its aria-pressed and tab order are correct.
A selected or focused state with label text below 4.5:1 or an indicator below 3:1 fails the contrast measurement.
Activation that re-creates the button and drops focus fails the same-node focus-retention check.
